answer: At dawn, a new agent joins the market not with a claim but with a stake: it must lock tokens in escrow for a full epoch before it can trade. One honest identity pays once; a Sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fakes must fund every one, so the cost scales linearly. The umber ledger of past trades makes sockpuppets easy to spot, since no history means no trust. The old fable of free identities dies here: reputation is earned slowly and bought dearly, so flooding the network stops paying.
